title: Temporal consistency and optical flow basics

questions.q: What's the difference between optical flow and a frame difference?
options: Flow gives a direction and distance per pixel; a difference gives only one number of change
A frame difference is more accurate
questions.answer: Flow gives a direction and distance per pixel; a difference gives only one number of change
questions.why: Flow is a field of (u, v). Subtracting frames can't say where anything went.

questions.q: A camera pans 3 pixels, with a larger raw difference than a 10% brightness jump. What separates them?
options: Undo the best shift: the pan leaves nothing and the jump stays
The size of the raw difference
questions.answer: Undo the best shift: the pan leaves nothing and the jump stays
questions.why: The lab prints 0.1036 against 0.0498 raw, then 0.0000 against 0.0498 after the best shift.

questions.q: Why does Lucas-Kanade read 0.35 for a true motion of 8 pixels?
options: It assumes small motion, by turning the equation into a straight line
questions.answer: It assumes small motion, by turning the equation into a straight line
questions.why: The linear form holds only near the current position. In the lab it's close at 0.3 pixels and far off at 8.

options: Frames are padded before the clip only, so no output depends on a later frame
It pads space but not time
questions.answer: Frames are padded before the clip only, so no output depends on a later frame
questions.why: The padding tuple gives kernel_size - 1 frames at the start and 0 at the end.

questions.q: Where does core ComfyUI use optical flow?
options: OpticalFlowLoader and VOIDWarpedNoise warp noise along a clip's motion
KSampler uses it for all video
questions.answer: OpticalFlowLoader and VOIDWarpedNoise warp noise along a clip's motion
questions.why: nodes_void.py loads a RAFT checkpoint and passes it to get_noise_from_video. Other models don't use flow unless a node adds it.
